title: Home Assistant health integration (Marketplace, HACS) | Life Dashboard
description: The Life Dashboard integration turns Health Connect or Apple Health data into Home Assistant sensors and statistics with all your history, paired by QR code.
h1: A Home Assistant integration for your phone's health data
lead: The Life Dashboard integration is an open-source Home Assistant integration, installed through the Marketplace (HACS before Home Assistant 2026.11), for the Life Dashboard Companion apps on Android and iPhone. One QR code pairs a phone, and every day lands in long-term statistics, as far back as the phone has data. No broker and no YAML.

highlights.title: Sensors for today
highlights.text: Day totals for steps, distance and calories, and the latest heart rate, sleep, weight and blood pressure, each with its source app.

highlights.title: All your history
highlights.text: Every day lands on its own date, so a backfill from the phone fills the Statistics graph card as far back as the phone has data.

highlights.title: Paired by QR code
highlights.text: One code per phone holds a webhook URL and a signing secret. The phone never gets a Home Assistant login or token.

highlights.title: Signed, always
highlights.text: HMAC-SHA256 on every payload, checked in constant time before parsing. There's no switch to turn signing off.

highlights.title: Nothing counted twice
highlights.text: The apps re-send on purpose. A repeat leaves sensors, day totals and sessions as they were; a correction replaces the old figure.

highlights.title: Back into Health Connect
highlights.text: Map a scale or blood pressure entity, and the Android app writes each new reading into Health Connect. Samsung Health and Google Health pick up weight and body fat from there.

highlights.title: Stable from 1.0.0
highlights.text: Within 1.x, an update keeps your entities, statistics, automations and pairing working. A change to any of that waits for 2.0.0.

sections.h2: Sleep, steps and heart rate sensors, with history behind them
sections.text: Sensors appear the first time their type arrives, so you only get what you sync. A sensor holds the latest value; long-term statistics hold the past, each value on the date it happened, as far back as the phone has data.

bullets.sub: Steps, distance, active and total calories, from Health Connect's or HealthKit's deduplicated figures.
Heart rate, resting heart rate, HRV, last sleep, weight, blood pressure, glucose, SpO2, VO2 max, the last workout and more, with measured_at and source.
Steps, distance in km, calories, sleep, exercise and mindfulness time in hours, hydration and screen time.

bullets.main: Mean, minimum and maximum per hour
bullets.sub: Heart rate, weight, blood pressure and the other measurements.
Adding a phone offers to take over the statistics of one you removed, so its graphs and running totals carry on instead of starting again.

sections.h2: Sleep stages per night, and a card that draws the night
sections.text: From version 1.1.0, each night becomes sensors and statistics for deep, light, REM, awake and time asleep, with one main night per wake date. The Life Dashboard Sleep Card, a separate install from the Marketplace, draws the newest night on your dashboard as a hypnogram. On Android it also works with the official Companion app, without Life Dashboard.

bullets.sub: last_sleep_asleep holds the hours asleep of the newest main night, with every stage in its stages attribute.
Hours of deep, light, REM, awake and asleep per night, for a chart per day, week or month. Send history from the app fills in older nights.
The session with the most time asleep. Naps and a second app that wrote the same night don't add up with it.

sections.h2: One QR code per phone, and a signature on every payload
sections.text: Add the integration once per phone, and it shows a QR code with a webhook URL and a secret it generated: 64 hex characters. A payload without a valid HMAC-SHA256 signature gets a 401 and is logged without its contents. How to add Health Connect to Home Assistant walks through the pairing.

bullets.main: Home address, public address or Home Assistant Cloud
bullets.sub: A home address keeps the data on your network, over plain HTTP unless you add TLS. A cloudhook syncs from anywhere without port forwarding, through Home Assistant Cloud's servers.
Readings sent back to the phone are signed and bound to the request, so nobody on the network can slip one in.
Download diagnostics redacts the secret and the webhook ID, and holds no health data.

sections.h2: A Health dashboard and theme to copy
sections.text: An example dashboard built only from Home Assistant's own cards, with a theme in the colors of the apps, so there are no custom cards to install. Paste it into a new dashboard, put in your phone's name and ID, and remove what your phone doesn't send. The screenshots show demo data from two made-up phones.

bullets.sub: Steps, distance, calories, workout time and heart rate as tiles, and the last workout with its pace, heart rate and laps.
Heart rate variability over 7 days against your 60-day baseline, resting heart rate over 7 days against the 7 before, and VO2 max.
Last night on a gauge, with the night's breathing, oxygen and skin temperature, sleep per night and the sleep stages per night.
Workout time per week and month, resting heart rate, steps and distance, and weight and body fat over a year.
A view with two phones side by side, an Android phone and an iPhone alike, and both in the same graphs.

sections.h2: Screen time per app, with its history
sections.text: On Android, the app sends screen time from the same usage statistics Digital Wellbeing reads. The example dashboard has a view of its own for it.

bullets.sub: Screen time in hours, the most used app, and the top five with their minutes.
Created disabled, up to 50 per phone, for automations such as a time limit on one game.
Every app whose sensor you enable gets a statistic with its time per day, so a graph shows it over weeks or a year.

requirements: Home Assistant 2026.3 or newer. From 2026.11 nothing else needs installing: the integration is in the Marketplace. Older versions need HACS, where it is in the default list. On each phone, Life Dashboard Companion for Android or for iPhone. Screen time, the sensors per app and Receive need the Android app.

faq.q: Should I use MQTT or this integration?
faq.a: Pick one; running both gives you two devices with the same numbers. MQTT Discovery creates the same sensors and suits a setup that already has a broker and only wants current values. Only the integration has backfilled history, a screen time sensor per app and readings back to the phone.

faq.q: Will an update break my automations?
faq.a: Not within 1.x. Version 1.0.0 comes with a written promise: an update keeps your entities, statistics, automations and pairing working, and a change to any of that waits for 2.0.0. What 1.x keeps stable lists what it covers. Coming from 0.x? Read the changelog first: 1.0.0 puts last sleep and screen time in hours and distance today in km, so an automation that reads minutes or metres needs an update.

faq.q: Can several phones share one Home Assistant?
faq.a: Yes. Add the integration once per phone, Android and iPhone alike. Each gets its own webhook ID, secret, device and statistics, and the entity IDs follow the name you give it, such as sensor.owen_s_pixel_steps_today.

Eight of the 34 Health Connect types are events: meals, mindfulness sessions, sexual activity and the five cycle tracking types. Workouts get a last workout sensor and the minutes of today and yesterday, and mindfulness counts as time per day, in hours, in the statistics. For the raw records, add a second webhook in the app that points at your own backend.

faq.q: Can Home Assistant send a scale reading to the phone?
faq.a: Yes, on Android. Configure maps one entity per type: weight, body fat, lean body mass, bone mass, body water mass, height and blood pressure. The app writes each new value into Health Connect, and Samsung Health and Google Health pick up weight and body fat from there. Blood pressure lands in Health Connect too, but Google Health doesn't read it and Samsung Health shows it only in some versions. Smart scale to Samsung Health has the setup.

faq.q: Can I see sleep stages in Home Assistant?
faq.a: Yes, from integration 1.1.0: deep, light, REM, awake and time asleep per night, as sensors and statistics. The sleep stages guide has the details and the Sleep Card that draws the night as a hypnogram.

faq.q: Does Home Assistant poll the phone or a cloud?
faq.a: No. The phone pushes a signed payload on its own schedule, and nothing in Home Assistant polls. A payload that fails while Home Assistant restarts waits in the app's outbox and goes out with the next sync.

faq.q: Can an AI read the history?
faq.a: Yes, a model you choose, through ha-mcp, a community MCP server for Home Assistant with a history tool that reads long-term statistics. Home Assistant's built-in MCP server only offers current states. With a local model nothing leaves your network; with a cloud model, your questions and the results go to its provider. Health Connect and Apple Health over MCP has the setup, and the stack's own MCP server if you'd rather keep the data in Postgres.

faq.q: What happens when I remove a phone?
faq.a: Deleting the entry removes the device and its sensors, deletes its cloudhook if it had one, and deletes the phone's files in .storage. Its long-term statistics stay in the recorder, as they do for any integration you remove. Add a phone later, and it offers to take them over, so the graphs and running totals carry on where they stopped.
